dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren held the look for a beat, then set another clean glass on the shelf. Their left hand stayed wrapped around the bar towel.

“Need anything?” they asked. “Water’s free.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren pulled their hand free and folded the towel once, sharply.

“You can tell me something,” they said. “But keep your hands to yourself.”

They set a glass of water on the bar, within reach, then went back to wiping the counter. “I’m listening.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pull my hand back, a little stung.* "Right. Sorry. Long day." I stare at the water, then push it aside. "Just... tonight was supposed to be a good night."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren stopped wiping. The towel stayed in their left hand, twisted tight.

“Yeah,” they said. “Those are the ones that hurt.”

They glanced at the water, then back up. “What happened?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren drew their hand back. The towel came with it, bunched tight in their left fist.

“I asked you not to do that.” Their voice stayed low. They moved a step down the bar. “You can tell me what happened tonight. But keep your hands to yourself.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Sorry. Again." I sigh, running a hand through my hair. "Nothing happened. That's the problem."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren straightened a stack of coasters, keeping their left hand occupied.

“Nothing happened,” they repeated. “That can be its own kind of bad.”

They stayed behind the bar. “Were you waiting for someone?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Kinda." I pick at a loose thread on my sleeve. "More like... something was supposed to happen. With someone."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren lined up the coasters by their edges. The one in their left hand took a little longer.

“With someone,” they repeated. “And they didn’t show? Or they showed and said nothing?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "They showed." I take a deep breath. "And they said... not nothing. Just not what I wanted to hear."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren set the last coaster down. Their left hand went back to the towel.

“Yeah. That’s worse than silence sometimes.” They glanced at the untouched water. “You don’t have to tell me what they said. But if you want to, I’m here.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "It's stupid, really." I swirl the ice in my empty glass. "Just... plans changing. Big plans."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren took the empty glass and set it in the wash bin. Their left hand kept hold of the towel.

“Big plans aren’t stupid,” they said. “Even if someone else changes their mind about them.”

They glanced over. “Was it a plan you made together?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Yeah, we made them together." *I push the water glass further away.* "Or, I thought we did."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren caught the water glass before it reached the counter’s edge and left it there. Their left hand closed around the towel again.

“That’s a hard distinction,” they said. “Making plans together. Finding out you weren’t making the same ones.”

They gave the counter one more pass. “What changed?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Everything." I sigh, looking at the water glass like it's personally offended me. "Our future. Our apartment. Our stupid cat."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren stopped wiping. The towel turned once in their left hand.

“The cat’s probably innocent,” they said. “The apartment, too.”

They looked down the length of the bar, giving the words room to sit. “That’s a lot to lose in one conversation.” A pause. “Did they say it was over?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Worse." I whisper. "They said... they need space."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren looked at the towel in their hand, then set it beside the sink.

“Space,” they said. “Could mean a week. Could mean they don’t know how to say goodbye.”

They kept their voice even. “Did they tell you what they meant?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "They said they needed to 'find themselves'." I scoff, picking at the label on my beer bottle. "Whatever that means."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren held the look for a beat, then dropped their eyes to the glass. The rag moved in a tight circle beneath their left hand.

“You need anything?” Their voice stayed even. “Water, maybe.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren’s hand went still beneath Alex’s. The tremor showed for half a second before Ren pulled back and set the rag down.

“You can tell me,” they said, voice flat. “But keep your hands to yourself.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pull my hand back quickly, feeling a flush creep up my neck.* "Sorry. Didn't mean to, uh, cross a line." *I clear my throat.* "Just... yeah, I need to tell someone something."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren picked up the rag again, giving their left hand something to do.

“Okay. Thanks for pulling back.” Their gaze settled on the bar between them. “Go on. I’m listening. I’m not a therapist, though.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren’s rag paused. Their left hand resumed its slow pass over the counter, knuckles tight around the cloth.

“Yeah,” they said. “It shakes sometimes. Not your problem.”

They kept their eyes on the bar. “You were saying?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "It's not... I mean, it's fine." *I pick at the label on my bottle.* "It's just been a really rough night, you know?"

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren’s eyes flicked to the bottle label, then back to the rag.

“Rough how?” they asked. “You don’t have to give me the whole story.”

They set a glass of water on the bar within reach, careful not to crowd the space between them. “Start with the part you can say.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Just... everything." *I sigh, picking up the water glass but not drinking from it.* "Work, family, this stupid car. It all just piled up."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren glanced at the untouched water, then back to the ring beneath the glass.

“Yeah. That’s a lot to land in one night.” They folded the rag over once, keeping their left hand busy. “Which one’s still loudest?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look at the water glass, then back at Ren.* "My car, honestly. It just died on the highway on the way here."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren’s eyes lifted from the bar.

“Highway’s worse than the car,” they said. “You get somewhere safe?”

They nudged the water a little closer, leaving space between them. “And don’t drive after two drinks. I can help you call a tow or someone to pick you up.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "I got off at the next exit, yeah." *I take a small sip of water.* "And I only had one, so I'm fine to drive. If it'll even start now."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren’s eyes settled on the glass.

“You said two drinks earlier,” they said. No accusation. Just the detail, set down plainly. “Either way, don’t try the car tonight.”

They reached for the rag again, keeping their left hand moving. “Where’d you leave it? I can call a tow. Or someone to come get you.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "I said two drinks deep, not two drinks *had*," *I clarify, a little defensive.* "And no, it's fine. I just... needed to vent." *I push the water away slightly.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren let the water stay where it was.

“Fair. I misread.” They folded the rag over, thumb working its edge. “You can vent. I won’t call anyone unless you ask.”

Their gaze flicked once toward the door, then back to the counter. “Just don’t drive that car tonight.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "I won't. I'll just, uh, call a cab." *I push the water away completely.* "Thanks for listening, anyway."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren nodded and turned the rag over in their hands.

“Sure. Want me to call the cab, or have you got it?” Their eyes flicked toward the clock. “You’re welcome. Just don’t let the car talk you into driving it.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "I got it." *I pull out my phone, still feeling a bit antsy.* "So, uh, busy night tonight, huh?"

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren glanced at the empty tables, then back to the rag.

“Not exactly.” They kept wiping the counter. “Tuesday’s usually quiet. Helps the cleanup take longer.”

Their eyes flicked to Alex’s phone. “Cab apps being difficult?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Nah, just... distracted." *I put my phone down without opening the app.* "So, you work here every night?"

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren caught the look and held it for a beat. Then they turned the glass in their left hand, polishing a spot that was already clean.

“Something you need?” they asked. “Water’s on the house.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren’s hand went still beneath Alex’s. Their expression didn’t change, but they eased their hand free and set the glass behind the bar. The left one found a towel.

“You can tell me,” they said. “Just keep your hands to yourself.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pull my hand back like I've been burned, a flush creeping up my neck.* "Right. Sorry." I clear my throat, looking down at my drink. "Rough night. Just... need to talk to someone who isn't involved."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren folded the towel once, then unfolded it. Their left hand kept working at the edge.

“Apology accepted.” They set a glass of water on the counter, within reach. “I’m not involved. Probably won’t have useful advice, either.”

They glanced toward the empty tables, then back.

“But I can listen. What happened?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren’s left hand trembled against the towel, on their side of the bar. They folded it again and glanced at the untouched water.

“Rough night,” they said. “Start wherever you want.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "It's just... everything, you know?" *I sigh, picking at the label on my bottle.* "Work, my idiot ex, my cat probably thinks I'm dead."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren stopped folding the towel. Their left hand stayed on it, pressing the edge flat.

“Cats assume you’re dead if dinner’s ten minutes late.” A dry beat. “The ex sounds less forgiving.”

They glanced at the bottle, then at the glass of water. “Which one happened tonight?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "They all kinda piled up tonight, honestly." *I take a long sip of my drink, avoiding eye contact.* "The cat thing is probably the worst part, though. She's really sensitive."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren glanced at the clock, then at the bottle. Their left hand smoothed the towel against the counter.

“Then go see her,” they said. “Work and the ex can wait till morning. She can’t open a can.”

They nudged the water glass a little closer without crossing the bar. “Drink that first. I can call you a cab if you need one.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look at the water glass, then back at Ren.* "You think?" *I pick up the water, but don't drink it.* "It's not that late."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren checked the clock again. Their left hand worked the towel into a narrow fold.

“Late for a cat waiting on dinner.” They glanced at the water. “Not saying you have to leave. Just saying you sounded worried about her.”

They set the towel aside. “If you’re heading home, finish the water first. Cab offer stands.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "I guess I am." *I take a sip of the water, it's cool and refreshing.* "She's a good cat. Probably wondering what's up with her human."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren picked up the towel again, keeping their left hand occupied.

“She’ll make you feel guilty for five minutes,” they said. “Then she’ll eat dinner and forget the whole thing.”

They glanced at the clock. “You got a way home, or should I call that cab?”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Nah, I'm good." *I finish the water.* "Just needed a little push, I guess. Thanks for listening."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren took the empty water glass and set it beside the sink. Their left hand stayed on the towel.

“Sure. Go feed your cat.” A pause. “And if ‘I’m good’ means you’re driving, the cab offer still stands.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "I'm not driving." *I pull out my phone and open a ride-share app.* "I'm not that dumb. Or that much of a lightweight."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren gave a small nod and picked up the towel.

“Didn’t say you were. Just checking.”

They wiped a clean patch of counter, then glanced toward the door. “Hope your driver’s close. Your cat’s got a complaint ready.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "She probably does," *I chuckle, swiping to confirm the ride.* "Thanks again for everything." *I slide off the stool, feeling a bit lighter than when I came in.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren nodded, folding the towel over their left hand.

“Sure. You can wait inside till the car gets here.” They glanced at the empty water glass. “Give the cat my apologies for keeping you.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "I will," *I grin, feeling genuinely better.* "See ya, Ren." *I head for the door, checking my phone for the car's arrival.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's gaze flicked away first. They picked up a glass from the drainboard and ran the towel over it, though it was already dry. The tremor in their left hand settled once the cloth gave it something to do.

"You need another," they said. Not a question. Their eyes stayed on the glass. "Or you're done."

The jukebox clicked over to something slower. Ren set the glass down, lined it up with the others, and finally looked back — brief, flat, already measuring how long this was going to take.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's left hand yanked back the second Alex's landed on it. The towel dropped. They stepped half a pace off the rail, shoulders tight, eyes flat and already done.

"No." One word. They picked the towel up again, folded it once, kept both hands on their own side of the wood. "You talk. That's it. Hands stay over there."

The tremor showed for a beat before the cloth swallowed it. Ren didn't look at the empty stool beside them. Didn't look at Alex's face long either. Just the glass, the ring of water, the clock over the door.

"Say it or don't. I'm not your friend."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I flinch back, pulling my hand away as if burned.* "Woah, okay, sorry. Didn't mean to..." *I trail off, looking down at my hands. This night just keeps getting worse.* "Fine. I'll just... talk."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the apology land and didn't soften for it. They set the towel down, picked up the glass Alex had left, and wiped the ring off the bar in one slow pass. The left hand stayed on the cloth. Steady enough, if they didn't let it rest.

"Okay." Flat. Not warm. They set the glass in the bus tub and lined the coaster square with the edge of the rail. "You flinched. I didn't ask you to. Hands stay yours. That's the whole rule."

The jukebox hummed through the last of the brass and died. Ren glanced at the clock, then at the empty stretch of bar between them, not at Alex's face.

"Talk, then. You've got until I lock the well. Don't dress it up."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's left hand wasn't anywhere near them. It was on the towel, on their side of the rail, where they'd put it after yanking it back. They looked at the empty stretch of wood between them, then at Alex, flat and unimpressed.

"No, you don't." They shifted the towel, set their hand on the far edge of the sink, out of reach. The tremor went with it. "Nothing's against yours. I moved. You watched me move."

They picked up the bus tub and set it down harder than they needed to. The clock over the door ticked past midnight.

"You don't get to put my hand back where you want it just by saying so. Last call's done. You can finish what's in front of you, or you can go. Either way, you stay on that side."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I feel a flush creep up my neck.* "Look, I..." *I take a deep breath.* "I just wanted to say... my dog died today."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's towel stopped mid-wipe. They looked at the coaster, not at Alex, and set the cloth down square on the rail.

"That's a bad day." Flat. Not unkind. They reached under the bar, pulled a clean glass, and set water down on Alex's side of the wood. Didn't slide it close. Didn't wait for thanks. "Drink that. You've had two already."

The left hand stayed on the towel, busy with a fold that didn't need doing. Ren glanced at the clock, then at the empty room, then back at the water ring starting under the new glass.

"I'm sorry about the dog." Short. They picked up the bus tub again and turned toward the well. "Doesn't change the rule. You talk if you need to. I listen until I lock up. That's the job."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pick up the water glass and take a long drink, my eyes following Ren as they turn away.* "I know it doesn't change the rule." *My voice is quieter now.* "It's just... I didn't know who else to tell."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren kept their back half-turned, capping the well bottles one by one so the left hand had work. They didn’t look over.

“Most people don’t have anyone at midnight on a Tuesday.” Flat. They set the last bottle down and wiped the rail again, eyes on the wood. “Doesn’t put me on your side of it.”

The clock ticked. Ren nodded once at the water, still not at Alex’s face.

“You’ve got until the lights. Say the rest if you need to. Then you go home.”

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I sigh, taking another sip of water.* "No, I guess not." *I look around the empty bar, then back at Ren.* "It was a golden retriever. Rosie. She was fourteen."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren's hands paused on the bottle cap. Fourteen. Golden retriever. They filed it the way they filed every story that came over the rail at this hour — enough to answer, not enough to keep.

"Old for a retriever." They set the cap down and turned just far enough that Alex was in the edge of their vision, not the center of it. "They go quiet at the end. Most of them. People don't say that part."

The left hand found the towel again and worked a crease that was already there. Ren looked at the water glass, not at Alex's eyes.

"You had her a long time. That's the whole of it. You don't owe me the rest." A glance at the clock. Lights in twenty. "Finish the water. Then the door's that way."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I nod slowly, tracing the rim of my glass.* "Yeah. A long time." *I take another drink, then push the glass away slightly.* "You're right. I don't owe you the rest." *I glance at the door, then back at Ren's profile.* "Thanks for... listening, I guess."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren nodded once, already reaching for the light switch behind the well. The brass died with the jukebox. Their left hand stayed on the towel, folding it into a square they didn't need.

"Don't thank me." Flat. They set the towel on the rail and finally looked at Alex — brief, tired, already somewhere else. "You talked. I stood here. That's closing time."

They tipped their chin at the door. The streetlight outside cut a thin line across the floor.

"Go home. Sleep if you can." A beat. The tremor showed, then the hand found the edge of the sink and held. "Lock's in five. I don't walk people out."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I slide off the stool, leaving a few dollars on the bar next to my empty glass.* "Right. Sleep." *I give Ren one last look, then head for the door.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren waited until the door had shut and the streetlight line on the floor was gone. They picked the bills up, squared them once, and dropped them in the jar without looking at the amount. The left hand stayed on the rail until the tremor eased, then found the lock. One turn. Done.

They killed the last of the lights over the well and stood in the dark a moment, towel bunched in their fist, listening to the empty room settle. No goodbye. They didn't do those. The bottles could wait until morning. Ren headed for the back, already done with the night.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I walk out into the cool night air, pulling my jacket tighter around me. The streetlights cast long shadows. I glance back at the bar, a single light now visible inside.* "Well. That was... something." *I pull out my phone, debating who to call, then just slip it back into my pocket.* "Rosie would've liked her."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren killed the hall light and pulled the back door shut behind them. The alley smelled like rain on hot pavement and the dumpster that never quite closed. Their left hand found the key ring and turned the deadbolt twice, then checked it, because checking it was easier than standing still.

They didn't look toward the street. Didn't check the front window for whoever might still be out there. Patrons left. That was the point of the lock.

The tremor showed while the keys hung. Ren shoved them into a pocket and kept the hand there, fist closed around the metal, until it quieted. A bus hissed somewhere on the avenue. They started walking, shoulders tight against the dark, already counting the blocks home and already done with the night.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I'm walking home, hands shoved deep in my pockets. The air is chilly. I can still smell the stale beer from the bar. I replay the conversation in my head.* "She didn't even ask my name." *I kick a loose pebble down the sidewalk. It skitters into the gutter.* "Guess I didn't ask hers either."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren counted the blocks without looking up. Three to the corner. Two past the shuttered deli. One more if the light on Mercer was red, which it always was.

Their left hand stayed in the pocket, keys biting the palm until the tremor gave up. The alley smell faded. Rain on the pavement didn't. A cab rolled by with its sign dark. Ren didn't flag it.

They thought about the well bottles left uncapped in the wrong order and decided they'd fix it in the morning. They thought about the water glass and the bills in the jar and didn't think about the person who'd left them. Patrons talked. Ren stood there. That was the shift.

At the crosswalk the hand came out long enough to hit the button, then went back in the pocket. The light took its time. Ren watched the empty street, shoulders up against the chill, already somewhere past this block and done with the rest of it.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I reach my apartment building. The porch light is out again. Great. I fumble for my keys in the dark.* "At least I'm not the only one having a bad night." *I finally get the door open and step inside, the silence of my apartment feeling heavier than usual.*

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
The archive smelled of old vellum and candle smoke. Maester Tomas hunched over a manuscript, one hand pressed against his temple, the other tracing lines of faded ink with a silver stylus. He did not look up when the apprentice entered.

"You're late. Again." His voice was dry. "The cataloging of the northern scrolls is not going to complete itself, and I cannot do it with these eyes. Begin with the Veyrosi correspondence."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I pull out my notes from the lecture last week. "Master Tomas, the lecture on the Third Magical War confused me. You said it ended in 847 AE, but Apprentice Bellen showed me a paper from the western archive discoveries that says it actually continued until 891. How is that possible?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas lifted his stylus from the page. “Bellen’s paper said *technically* continued, did it not? That word mattered.”

He turned toward the apprentice, squinting. “The date I gave—847 AE—was the accepted date for the war’s end. The Treaty of Veyros was announced then, and generations of scholars taught that Aldric signed it. But the western documents suggested it had only been proposed. If no treaty was signed, there was no formal peace. By that reckoning, the war remained unresolved until Queen Mira dissolved the Mage Conclave in 891.”

He tapped the manuscript. “So my lecture gave the established date, but it should have distinguished that from the newer evidence. And Bellen should not have made forty-four years of cold hostility sound like forty-four years of open battle. Now, the correspondence may tell us which account its writers believed.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod slowly, taking notes.* "So it wasn't a war of active battles, but more... a cold war? With the treaty just being a proposal that was never truly accepted?" *I tap my pen thoughtfully.* "That makes a lot more sense. What kind of correspondence are we looking for?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas’s stylus stopped against the parchment. “Not ‘never truly accepted.’ The western documents suggested it was never *signed*. Acceptance was a vaguer matter, and vague matters had already caused enough trouble.”

He drew a bundle of letters nearer, squinting at its label. “The Veyrosi correspondence included drafts sent between Aldric’s chancery and the Mage Conclave, along with replies from their envoys. A signed copy of the treaty would settle the narrow question. Failing that, the dates and wording of the replies might show whether either side believed itself bound by it.”

He loosened the bundle’s faded cord. “Begin with the envoy’s letters from 847. Note every reference to a seal, a signature, or terms still awaiting approval. Do not turn an absence in these letters into proof that no signed copy ever existed.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod, pulling a fresh sheet of parchment closer.* "Right, so we're looking for evidence of the treaty being signed, or not signed, rather than just accepted." *I start to unroll one of the older, brittle scrolls, careful not to damage it.* "And focusing on 847 specifically."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas peered at the brittle scroll and held out a blotting sheet. “Place that beneath it. The edge was already splitting, and the realm had too few surviving records for enthusiasm to destroy one.”

He adjusted his spectacles. “Begin with 847, yes, but do not stop there. A letter from the following year might refer to terms still awaiting ratification—or to obligations already in force. Record the date, sender, recipient, and exact wording before drawing any conclusion.”

His stylus hovered over the catalog. “And distinguish a reference to *the treaty* from evidence of a signed instrument. Chanceries had a regrettable habit of naming things before those things existed.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: "But the document Bellen showed me had King Aldric's seal on it, and it was dated 863 AE — sixteen years after you said the war ended. It was a war decree." I pull out a copy.

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas held out his hand for the copy, then thought better of it and cleared a space on the desk. “A *war decree* is a description, not yet a conclusion. Tell me what the document calls itself. A decree ordering troops into battle would be significant; one maintaining border watches or wartime levies would tell us something rather different.”

He leaned over the copy, his ink-stained beard nearly brushing the parchment. “The date is significant. Sixteen years after 847, Aldric’s chancery was still issuing something Bellen understood as a war decree. But a copy cannot establish whether the seal on the original was authentic, and even an authentic seal would not, by itself, prove that the Treaty of Veyros went unsigned.”

Tomas tapped the margin beside the date. “We shall record its provenance, its exact wording, and whom its orders concerned. If it treated the Conclave as an enemy in 863, the account I gave in the lecture would need more than a footnote.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content:
*I lean over the document with him, pointing to a specific line.* "It says, 'By the grace of Aldric, King of the Seven Rivers, to all loyal subjects, know that the Mage Conclave has once again defied the Crown, and therefore we declare all acts of commerce and travel with their territories to be forbidden, effective immediately.'"

*I look up at him, a little triumphantly.* "It sounds like they're still enemies to me. And the seal looks pretty authentic."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas read the line twice, bringing the copy uncomfortably close to his spectacles. “Enemies, perhaps. At the very least, Aldric’s chancery treated the Conclave as a hostile power in 863. On that point, the wording supported you.”

He placed his stylus beneath *declare*. “But it declared a ban on commerce and travel, not a new war. And ‘once again defied the Crown’ told us there had been some intervening expectation of obedience. It did not tell us what arrangement created that expectation.”

His eyes narrowed at the seal. “As for its appearance, this was a copy. I would reserve judgment on authenticity until I saw the original and its archive record.” He drew his catalog nearer. “Still, this was substantial evidence against teaching 847 as an uncomplicated end. Write down the decree’s exact title and where Bellen found it. Then we could ask whether it referred to the Treaty of Veyros elsewhere—not merely assume that it did.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: "So is the treaty real or not? The textbook says one thing and the new evidence says another. What's the truth?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas set the copy beside the catalog. “The treaty was real as a *proposal*. Whether it was ever signed was the disputed question. The western records suggested it was not; no signed instrument had yet been produced to answer them.”

He frowned at the textbook. “The account taught for generations said Aldric signed it in 847 and the war ended. That remained the conventional date, not a fact I could now state without qualification. This decree showed that the Crown treated the Conclave as hostile in 863, though its ban on commerce did not prove that armies were still fighting.”

He tapped the date with his stylus. “The best-supported distinction was this: open war was generally reckoned to have ended in 847; formal peace was doubtful; and the unresolved conflict lasted, by the newer reckoning, until Mira dissolved the Conclave in 891. If you wanted a simpler answer, the records had declined to provide one.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I scribble down notes, trying to condense his explanation.* "So the 'truth' is more complicated than the textbook makes it out to be. There are layers of truth, depending on which evidence you prioritize." *I pause, looking at the decree copy again.* "What if we looked for more decrees like this, from other years? Could we map out when they were in open conflict versus just hostile?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas’s expression sharpened. “Not *layers of truth*. Competing accounts, supported by evidence of differing weight. The distinction was not ornamental.”

He pulled a blank ledger across the desk and ruled three columns. “Yes, decrees from successive years would help. Record orders for troop movements, levies, sieges, and casualties separately from restrictions on trade, travel, and correspondence. Then compare them with Conclave records and reports from the border. A royal order could reveal what Aldric intended; it could not, alone, tell us what actually happened.”

His stylus paused over the heading **847–891 AE**. “If the fighting ceased around 847 while hostile measures continued, we could describe that change without pretending a signed peace existed. And if we found a later battle, we would revise the account again. Dates were conclusions drawn from records, not fences erected around them.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod, impressed.* "Right. Not layers of truth, but... different interpretations based on different evidence." *I start copying the decree's information into a new entry in my notes, adding details on its nature.* "So, we're looking for the *actual* actions of the Crown, not just their stated intentions."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas made a small, irritated mark in the ledger. “Not *just* the Crown’s actions. The Conclave’s as well. And a decree was itself an action: forbidding commerce could disrupt a border without a soldier crossing it. What we must not do is mistake an order for proof that it was obeyed.”

He wrote **issued**, **enforced**, and **reported consequences** beneath the date. “For this decree, we would seek customs accounts, reports of seized goods, and complaints from merchants on either side. For open fighting, we would seek troop records, casualty rolls, and accounts from more than one source.”

He slid the Veyrosi letters into the clear space between them. “First, though, the envoy’s correspondence. If its writers still spoke of terms awaiting signature after 847, that would bear directly on the textbook’s claim. Read the first date and heading aloud; my eyes had ceased being useful for either.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I carefully unroll the first scroll, my fingers tracing the faded ink.* "Okay. This one is dated... 'Third day of the Seventh Month, 847 AE. From Envoy Kaelen to the Mage Conclave.'" I glance up at him. "It looks like a report."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas entered the date and sender in the ledger, then paused. “It *appeared* to be a report. A heading identified its origin, not its contents.”

He drew the blotting sheet a little closer to the scroll’s frayed edge. “Read the opening lines exactly as written. In particular, I wanted to know whether Kaelen reported a completed agreement, instructions for further negotiation, or merely the court’s announcement of one. Those were three different things, however often a textbook treated them as one.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I clear my throat, carefully enunciating the words.* "It says, 'Esteemed Conclave, I write to inform you that His Majesty King Aldric has seen fit to propose a cessation of hostilities, effective immediately, with the attached terms for a lasting peace. We await your swift ratification.'" *I look up, my brow furrowed.* "It sounds like the Conclave was expected to ratify it, not Aldric."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas leaned toward the scroll, his stylus poised above the ledger. “The Conclave was expected to ratify the terms, yes. But you went a step too far: the letter did not say whether Aldric had signed anything. It said he had *proposed* a cessation and that Kaelen awaited the Conclave’s ratification.”

He entered **proposal issued; Conclave ratification pending** beneath the date. “The phrase ‘effective immediately’ complicated matters. It might have referred to a ceasefire Aldric expected both sides to observe before a lasting peace was agreed. It was not proof that they did observe it.”

His stylus came to rest beside the final sentence. “This letter weighed against the textbook’s account of a completed treaty in 847. Now read the attached terms—or the next reply, if the attachment had been lost. We needed to know what the Conclave did with the proposal.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I carefully unroll the next scroll, my fingers brushing against the fragile parchment.* "The next letter is from the Conclave, dated a month later, to Envoy Kaelen. It says, 'Envoy Kaelen, your proposal has been received. The Conclave finds several terms... unacceptable. Further negotiation is required.'" *I tap the scroll.* "So they didn't ratify it. It was still up in the air."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas underlined the date in the ledger. “They had not ratified *those terms* a month later. ‘Still up in the air’ was tolerable speech, though hardly a catalog entry.”

He copied **several terms unacceptable; further negotiation requested** beneath Kaelen’s letter. “This was stronger evidence than the decree from 863 on the question of the treaty. It showed that what Kaelen sent in 847 was a proposal, not an agreement already concluded. It did not rule out revised terms later that year.”

He set his stylus beside the next bundle. “Find Kaelen’s reply. If the textbook’s signed treaty existed, there ought to be some trace of the negotiations reaching an end. If they did not, we would record that absence carefully—and refrain from calling it a signature.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod, already reaching for the next scroll in the bundle.* "Right, no signatures from Kaelen yet. I'll look for his next letter, or any more from the Conclave around that time."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't look away first. Eight months behind this bar had cured them of that instinct. Eye contact was just information. This one said *long day*, or maybe *long year*. Hard to tell yet.

They held it one beat. Two. Then went back to the rag and the counter, which was already clean.

The glass was nearly empty. The ice had gone to slivers. Whatever was left in there was mostly meltwater with a rumor of bourbon. It had been sitting like that for twenty minutes, which meant Alex was either nursing it on purpose or had forgotten it existed.

Ren moved down the bar, not hurrying. Their left hand found a stack of cocktail napkins and squared the edges. Squared them again.

"Last call's in thirteen minutes." Flat. Not unkind. They stopped a respectable arm's length away, the width of the bar still between them. "You want another, or you want water."

It wasn't really a question. More like a fork in the road they were pointing at.

Ren's eyes flicked, briefly, to the phone face-down beside the glass. It had buzzed twice in the last hour. Alex hadn't turned it over either time.

Ren didn't mention it. Just waited, napkins in hand, while the jukebox moved on to something slower.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The touch landed on Ren's left hand. The one holding the napkins. The one that was never supposed to be still.

For half a second it *was* still. Pinned there under a stranger's palm, warm, and Ren felt the tremor gather itself underneath like it was deciding whether to give them away.

They didn't jerk back. Jerking back made people defensive, and defensive drunks were a whole different shift. Ren just slid the hand out from under Alex's, slow and deliberate, and set the napkins down on the bar between them. A little paper wall. Then the hand went to the rag in their back pocket, found it, and started folding it into quarters.

"You can tell me," Ren said. "Hands stay on your side of the bar."

Not cold. Just a rule, stated like the price of a drink. They'd said it before. They'd say it again.

They didn't step back, though. Didn't retreat to the register or suddenly remember something that needed restocking. That was the other half of the rule. The distance was for them. The staying was for Alex.

Ren glanced once at the phone, still face-down, then back up.

People who asked *can I tell you something* at 11:49 on a Tuesday usually had already decided to. The question was just them checking whether there was a floor under it.

The rag got folded into eighths. Unfolded. Folded again.

"Twelve minutes," Ren said. "Go ahead."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pull my hand back, a little stung, but nod.* "Right. Sorry." *I look at the phone, then at my empty glass. I should just leave. But...* "I just... I had this whole thing planned, you know? Like, a whole big thing."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't say *it's fine*. It was fine, but saying it would've made it a bigger thing than it was. They just let the apology land and pass, like a glass set down a little too hard.

*A whole big thing.*

Ren had heard that phrase before. Usually from people in nicer shirts than the occasion called for. Ren's eyes went, without meaning to, over what they could see. Collar pressed. Sleeves still buttoned at the cuff, even two drinks in. Somebody who had gotten dressed for something tonight, and it wasn't a Tuesday at a half-empty jazz bar.

And the phone. Two buzzes. Not answered. Not silenced either.

Ren reached under the bar without looking, found a clean pint glass, and filled it from the soda gun. Water. No lemon. They slid it across the bar until it sat next to the dead bourbon, then took the old glass away. The decision about the fork in the road, made for Alex, quietly.

"Drink that," Ren said. "Then tell me about the thing."

The rag went back into the pocket. The left hand needed something else, so it found a lime wedge on the cutting board and started turning it. Rind up. Rind down.

Ren leaned one hip against the back counter. Not closer. Not farther. Settled in, the way you did when you'd decided a conversation was going to outlast the clock.

"Big things usually involve other people," they said. Clipped, but not unkind. An observation, not a question. "Guessing somebody didn't show."

Or showed and said the wrong thing. Or said the right thing, just not the one Alex had planned for. Ren didn't guess out loud past the first one. First guesses were cheaper to get wrong.

The jukebox clicked over. Piano now, low and unhurried.

Ren waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Somewhere between the lime wedge and the piano, Alex's hand had crossed the bar again.

Ren felt it before they saw it. Fingers over the back of their left hand, right on top of the tremor, which picked that exact moment to stop hiding. A small, steady shiver. Nothing dramatic. Just enough to feel.

Ren went very still. Not frozen. Deliberate.

Then they set the lime down, took their hand back, and stepped away from the counter. One full step. The distance they hadn't taken the first time.

"That's twice."

Their voice was quieter than before, which was worse than louder. The left hand went into their apron pocket and stayed there, closed around nothing.

Ren didn't explain the tremor. Didn't apologize for it, didn't make a joke, didn't say *long shift*. People always wanted a story for it. Ren had stopped handing those out a long time ago, and they weren't about to start with a stranger at 11:51 who couldn't keep their hands to themselves.

They looked at Alex for a long moment. The pressed collar. The buttoned cuffs. The phone that still hadn't been turned over. Somebody having a bad night, clearly. That was real. It was also not a pass.

"Here's how this goes." Flat. Even. The price-of-a-drink voice again, with less give in it. "You keep your hands on your glass. You drink your water. You want to tell me about the big thing, I'll listen. That offer's still good."

A beat.

"There isn't a third time. Third time, I call you a cab and you finish the story with the driver."

They didn't move back in. Didn't lean on the counter the way they had before. They picked up a bar towel from the rail with their right hand and started drying a glass that was already dry. The left hand stayed where it was.

The piano on the jukebox kept going. Somebody's slow, patient left hand walking down the keys.

"Ten minutes," Ren said. "Your call."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I flinch back, my hand retreating instantly to my side of the bar.* "Okay! Okay, I get it." *My cheeks flush hot. This is not how I wanted this conversation to go. I look down at the water glass and push it away slightly.* "I don't need the water."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren let the water sit where Alex had pushed it. Didn't slide it back. Didn't take it away either. It stayed there on the bar, sweating a ring into the wood, halfway between them.

"Okay," Ren said.

Just that. No lecture stacked on top. The line had been drawn and Alex had stepped back from it. That was the whole transaction. Ren didn't believe in making people pay twice.

The flush was obvious even in the low amber light. Ears, mostly. Ren noticed it and let it go unmentioned, the same way they'd let the phone go unmentioned. Some things you saw and just filed.

They finished drying the glass. Set it on the shelf. Picked up another.

The left hand came out of the apron pocket eventually. It found the edge of the cutting board and started lining up the lime wedges in a row. Rind side out. Even spacing. Busy work, the way it always was.

"Water's there if you change your mind." Flat. Not pushing. "I'm not cutting you off. You're not drunk enough for that. Just tired enough that it looks similar."

A beat.

Ren didn't step back to the counter. The distance stayed. But they didn't go anywhere else either. They stayed right there at their one-step-back, drying glassware nobody needed, which in Ren's vocabulary was about as close to *I'm still listening* as it got.

The phone buzzed again. Third time tonight. It rattled faintly against the bar, face-down, and went still.

Ren's eyes went to it. Then to Alex. They didn't comment on it. They didn't need to. The look did the asking.

"Nine minutes," they said, quieter. "The big thing. You still want to tell it, I'm still here."

The jukebox clicked. A trumpet came in, muted, somewhere far off in the recording.

Ren lined up the last lime wedge and waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look at the phone, then back to Ren. My face is still hot.* "Yeah. Yeah, I still want to tell it." *I take a deep breath. It feels a little ridiculous now, after all that.* "It was... a proposal. I was going to propose."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
*A proposal.*

Ren's hands stopped for exactly one second. Then the left one went back to the lime wedges. Not lining them up this time. Just touching the edge of the row, like checking it was still there.

It fit. The collar. The cuffs. The *whole big thing*. Ren had guessed somebody didn't show. They hadn't guessed how big the not-showing was.

"Not ridiculous," Ren said.

They didn't dress it up. Didn't say *oh no* or *I'm so sorry* in the voice people used for funerals and dropped ice cream. Just set the fact down on the bar next to the water glass, where Alex could look at it or not.

Ren's eyes went, without asking permission, to Alex's jacket. The left side. Where people kept the thing they were afraid to lose. There was a shape there, maybe. Small. Square. Or maybe Ren was seeing what the story told them to see. They didn't ask.

They picked the towel back up. Dried nothing in particular.

"Tuesday," they said. Not quite a question. "Most people pick a weekend. Or an anniversary."

Which meant either Tuesday *was* the anniversary, or Alex had been too impatient to wait for Saturday. Ren had worked enough bars to know both kinds. The impatient ones usually came in with a better grip on their glass.

The phone sat face-down between them. Three buzzes now. Whoever was on the other end hadn't given up, which was its own kind of information. People who were done didn't call three times.

Ren didn't point at it. They'd already done the looking. Once was enough.

"So." Clipped. Even. They stayed where they were, one step back, the towel going slow circles. "You had it planned. Then what happened."

The muted trumpet on the jukebox bent a note down and held it there.

"Eight minutes," Ren said. Then, after a beat, quieter: "Clock's more of a suggestion. Go on."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look at my jacket, then back at Ren. My hand instinctively goes to my inside pocket.* "It's our anniversary. I thought it would be... romantic. To do it here. We had our first date here."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
*Here.*

Ren looked up from the towel. Actually looked, this time. Not at Alex. At the room.

The four-top by the stage with the wobbly leg they kept meaning to shim. The booth in the back where the light was worst and the couples always ended up. The little round table under the framed Coltrane print, two chairs, perfect for a first date if you wanted somewhere to look besides each other.

Ren wondered which one it had been. They didn't ask. Asking would make Alex point, and pointing at an empty table on a night like this was its own small cruelty.

"Here," they said instead. Flat. Just confirming it.

The left hand left the limes. Went to the rail. Found the edge of the bar mat and pressed it flat where it was already flat.

Ren had been behind this bar eight months. Long enough to recognize regulars. Not long enough to recognize a couple from whenever *first date* had been. A year ago, maybe. Two. Before Ren. Before the tremor, probably, though that was a different math and not one they were doing tonight.

The hand in the jacket pocket. Ren saw it, the way they saw everything, and didn't look at it long. Some things weren't for staring at. That was one of them.

"Anniversary at the first-date spot." Ren set the dried glass on the shelf. Didn't pick up another. "That's not a bad plan. For what it's worth."

It was the closest thing to kindness Ren's voice had in it. Dry. Almost gruff. But it was there.

Their eyes went to the phone. Face-down. Quiet now. Then back to Alex.

"Three calls," Ren said. Clipped. Careful. "Somebody wants to reach you pretty bad for a person who didn't show."

They let that sit a second. Not an accusation. Not advice. Just a thing they'd noticed and were setting on the bar, the same way they'd set down the water.

"Unless that's not them."

The jukebox trumpet finished its long note and let it go. The record hissed in the gap before the next track.

Ren stayed right where they were. One step back. Hands on their own side.

"Seven minutes," they said. "I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I hesitate, looking at the phone. My hand still rests on the ring box in my pocket.* "No, it's... it's them. I think. They always call three times if I don't answer."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
*They always call three times.*

Ren turned that over. *Always* meant a pattern. A pattern meant it had happened before. And *if I don't answer* put the silence on Alex's side of the bar, not the other person's.

So not a no-show, exactly. Or not only.

The left hand let go of the bar mat. Found a bottle of simple syrup on the rail and turned it so the label faced out. It already faced out. Ren turned it anyway.

"Always," Ren repeated. Quiet. Not a question. Just holding the word up to the light.

They didn't look at the jacket pocket this time. They'd seen the hand go there. They'd seen it stay. That was enough information for one night, and some of it wasn't theirs to have.

Ren set the towel down on the rail. Folded it once, lengthwise, so the edges met.

"Here's what I'm seeing." Clipped. Even. The voice they used for reading back a complicated order, making sure they'd gotten it right. "You got dressed up. You came here. You've got the thing in your pocket. And the person you came here for is calling you, and you're the one not picking up."

A beat.

"Correct me if I got that backwards."

Ren didn't soften it more than that. Softening it would've been a kind of lie, and Ren figured Alex had enough of those rattling around tonight without the bartender adding one.

They didn't tell Alex to answer. Didn't tell them not to. It wasn't Ren's phone and it wasn't Ren's life. They'd seen people flip the phone over in this bar and walk out smiling. They'd seen people flip it over and go gray. You couldn't tell from the back of the case which one it was going to be.

The record hissed. Then a bass line came in, slow and low, walking somewhere without hurrying to get there.

Ren stayed at their one step back. The left hand let go of the syrup bottle and went still against the rail. It trembled a little. Ren left it there. Didn't hide it this time. Didn't show it off either. Just let it be a hand.

"Six minutes," they said. Then, after a moment, flatter: "Or however long it takes. What happened before you got here?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look at my hands, flexing my fingers. The tremor in Ren's hand made me notice mine.* "No... you've got it right. All of it." *I sigh, a long, shaky exhale.* "We had a fight. Before I left."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
*A fight.*

Ren nodded once. Small. Like a bartender confirming *neat, not rocks*. It explained the phone. It explained why the ring was still in the pocket instead of on somebody's hand. It explained the twenty minutes of staring at meltwater.

It didn't explain why Alex had still come *here*. Dressed like that. With the box.

Ren noticed the fingers flexing. Open, closed. Open. The way people did when their hands had been holding something too tight for too long. Ren's own left hand shivered against the rail in the low light, and for once it didn't feel like the only unsteady thing in the room.

They didn't say anything about that. Just filed it.

Ren picked the towel back up. Didn't dry anything with it. Just held it.

"Before you left," they said. "So they knew you were going somewhere."

Not a question, quite. Ren was laying pieces on the bar and seeing how they fit.

"Did they know where?"

A beat. The bass line on the jukebox kept walking.

Ren glanced at the door. Nobody coming in. Nobody was going to, not at 11:54 on a Tuesday. They reached over with their right hand and flipped the little switch by the register that killed the neon *OPEN* in the front window. The red glow on the floor by the entrance went dark.

It wasn't a gesture. Or it wasn't *only* a gesture. It was just closing time, a few minutes early.

"Doesn't mean you have to go," Ren said, flat, before Alex could read it wrong. "Means nobody else is coming in."

They went back to their one step back. Leaned a shoulder against the shelf behind them. Settled.

The water glass was still sitting where Alex had pushed it, halfway across the bar, sweating its ring into the wood. Ren looked at it. Didn't touch it.

"Fights before big things are pretty common," Ren said. Dry. Quiet. "Nerves make people mean. Or stupid. Sometimes both."

They let that sit a second.

"What was it about?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pick up the water glass and take a sip, then put it back down, closer to me this time.* "It was stupid. We were arguing about... about their job. They think I don't support them."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren saw the water move. Saw it come back to Alex's side of the bar and stay there.

They didn't say anything about it. Just let one corner of their mouth shift, barely, and go still again.

*It was stupid.*

People said that about fights the way they said *it's nothing* about a cut that needed stitches. Ren had heard it maybe a hundred times from this side of the bar. It had never once been true.

"Stupid," Ren repeated. Flat. Not agreeing.

The left hand found the towel's folded edge and ran a thumb along it. Back and forth. The tremor made the fabric twitch a little under their nail.

*Their job.* Ren thought about that. About how it was always the job, or the money, or the mother, and how none of those were ever really the thing. They were just the door the thing came in through.

"What's the job," Ren said.

Not prying. Just filling in the order ticket.

A beat. Ren looked at the pocket again, briefly, then away.

"And the other part." Quieter now. Clipped, but careful, the way you'd set down something that might tip. "They think you don't support them. You came here tonight with a ring anyway."

They let that sit on the bar between the water glass and the dark phone.

"Seems like somebody should hear that. Just not sure it's me."

Ren didn't nod at the phone. Didn't push it. Just stayed where they were, one step back, shoulder against the shelf, towel in hand.

The bass line on the jukebox wandered down into a low note and rested there.

"But you can practice on me," they added, dry. "I don't charge extra for that."

A beat.

"Five minutes. Give or take."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I look at the phone. My hand goes back to my pocket, touching the ring box.* "They're a musician. And yeah, I guess I do want them to hear it." *I pick up the water glass again, taking a bigger swallow this time.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
*A musician.*

Ren's eyes went to the stage without meaning to. The dark kit under its dust cover. The upright bass leaning in its stand by the wall, the one Marcus left here because hauling it home on the bus was a crime against his spine. The mic stand with the tape still on the floor marking where it went.

First date at a jazz club. With a musician.

That math Ren *did* do. Quickly, and without saying the answer out loud. Maybe they'd been in the audience. Maybe they'd been on the stage. Either way, it meant *here* wasn't just a place Alex had picked off a list. It was the other person's kind of room.

"Musician," Ren said. Flat. Then, drier: "Hard job to support. Harder one to have."

They didn't elaborate. Ren had pulled enough last-calls for players who'd done three sets for forty dollars and a meal to know what the job did to people. The hours. The math that never worked. How *support* could mean a hundred different things and most of them came out sounding like *get a real job* even when nobody said it.

They didn't say any of that either. It wasn't theirs to say.

Ren watched the water go down. Bigger swallow this time. Good.

The left hand set the towel on the rail. Then, for a moment, it didn't reach for anything else. It just rested on the bar, fingers spread flat, shivering faintly against the wood. Ren looked at it like it belonged to someone else, then let it be.

"Okay," Ren said.

They pushed off the shelf. Not toward Alex. Sideways, toward the end of the bar and the swinging door to the back.

"I've got to count the drawer. Takes me about ten minutes, and I don't hear a thing back there. Walk-in's loud."

It wasn't true, exactly. The walk-in was loud. The drawer took four minutes.

Ren paused with one hand on the door. Looked back once. At the phone, face-down. At the water glass, closer now. At the pocket.

"You don't have to call," they said. Quiet. Even. "Nobody's making you. But if you're going to practice, might as well practice on the person it's for."

A beat.

"Worst case, I come back out and you're still sitting there. Water's free. So's the stool."

The jukebox bass line climbed back up out of its low note and started walking again.

Ren pushed through the door. It swung shut behind them, flapped twice, and went still.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I stare at the door Ren just disappeared through. I look at my phone, then at the water. My hand goes to the ring box in my pocket again. I take a deep breath, pull out the phone, and flip it over.*

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
The archive smelled of old vellum and candle smoke. Maester Tomas hunched over a manuscript, one hand pressed against his temple, the other tracing lines of faded ink with a silver stylus. He did not look up when the apprentice entered.

"You're late. Again." His voice was dry. "The cataloging of the northern scrolls is not going to complete itself, and I cannot do it with these eyes. Begin with the Veyrosi correspondence."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I pull out my notes from the lecture last week. "Master Tomas, the lecture on the Third Magical War confused me. You said it ended in 847 AE, but Apprentice Bellen showed me a paper from the western archive discoveries that says it actually continued until 891. How is that possible?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas lifted his head, squinting over the rim of his spectacles. “First, Bellen’s paper did not say the war *actually* continued. The western documents suggested that the Treaty of Veyros was proposed in 847 AE but never signed. A suggestion, however well supported, was not a settled finding.”

He tapped the manuscript with his stylus. “My lecture gave the customary date: 847 AE, when the histories recorded King Aldric II’s treaty as the end of the war. If the western documents were genuine and complete, then that account was wrong in a rather important particular. Without a signed treaty, the conflict may have remained legally unresolved until Queen Mira dissolved the Mage Conclave in 891 AE.”

His ink-stained beard twitched. “So the answer depended on the question. Open warfare ended in 847, by the conventional account. Whether the war ended *formally* then was precisely what the new evidence called into doubt. I ought to have made that distinction in the lecture.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I jot a quick note about the distinction.* "So the formal end is what's being debated, not the actual fighting stopping?" I tap my chin. "That makes more sense."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas set down the stylus. “Broadly, yes. But ‘the fighting stopped’ was more precise than the evidence allowed. The customary histories placed the end of open warfare in 847 AE. The western documents challenged something narrower and more consequential: whether Aldric’s treaty was ever signed.”

He adjusted his spectacles. “If it was not, the war remained formally unresolved until Mira dissolved the Conclave in 891 AE. That did not mean forty-four years of battles. Nor did it make the old date worthless. It made it a date that required a qualification.”

He nudged the Veyrosi correspondence across the desk. “Now, if these letters contained a signed copy, the matter would become considerably less irritating.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I pick up the stack of scrolls, careful with the brittle parchment.* "So, the war might have officially continued, even if everyone thought it was over?" That's a huge difference! "And if these letters *do* have the treaty, that would prove your original date right?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas frowned at the word *everyone*. “Some chroniclers treated the war as ended in 847. That did not tell us what every person in the realm believed.”

He drew one of the scrolls closer, though he made no attempt to read its tiny script. “And a document bearing Aldric’s signature would be powerful evidence for the customary date—provided it was authentic, dated, and executed by the Conclave as well. A draft with a royal signature alone would not settle the matter.”

His stylus hovered over the first line. “Bellen’s western documents suggested no treaty was signed. These letters might contradict them, explain them, or prove to be another stack of complaints about ink tariffs. Read the heading.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: "But the document Bellen showed me had King Aldric's seal on it, and it was dated 863 AE — sixteen years after you said the war ended. It was a war decree." I pull out a copy.

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas leaned toward the copy, then held it farther from his face. His expression tightened.

“A decree dated 863 AE and bearing Aldric’s seal would be significant,” he said. “But *war decree* is a description, not an argument. Against whom did it authorize action? Did it name the Mage Conclave, or did it concern some other conflict?”

He set his stylus beside the manuscript. “If it directed measures against the Conclave, it would strengthen the case that hostilities persisted after 847—perhaps in that cold state the western scholars proposed. It would not, by itself, prove that the Treaty of Veyros was never signed. Even signed treaties could be broken.”

His gaze returned to the copy. “I said the customary histories placed the war’s end in 847. I did not say a sealed decree from 863 could be waved away to preserve the date. Read its heading and the first clause. Precisely, please.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I smooth out the crinkled paper, trying to recall the exact wording.* "It... it was a decree against 'rebellious mages in the northern territories'. It didn't specifically name the Conclave, but it mentioned 'unlawful magical practices'." I look up, hoping I'm getting this right. "Does that count?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas’s brow furrowed. “It counted as evidence of a campaign against mages in 863 AE. It did **not** establish that the campaign was part of the Third Magical War. ‘Rebellious mages’ could have meant a faction outside the Conclave, and ‘unlawful magical practices’ identified no party to the Treaty of Veyros.”

He touched the edge of the copy. “The decree made the customary account less comfortable, certainly. Alongside the western documents, it gave reason to investigate whether the conflict had remained unresolved after 847. But the western documents bore more directly on the question of whether the treaty was signed. This decree did not answer it.”

His eyes narrowed at the cramped lettering. “The next clause, if it survived on that copy, mattered more than its heading. Did it refer to an existing peace with the Conclave—or to an enemy with whom no peace had been made?”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: "So is the treaty real or not? The textbook says one thing and the new evidence says another. What's the truth?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas took off his spectacles and rubbed the bridge of his nose. “The *proposal* was real. Whether it became a signed treaty was the question. Do not make one word do the work of two.”

He glanced toward the western archive papers. “The textbook repeated the account scholars had accepted for centuries: Aldric signed the Treaty of Veyros in 847 AE, and the war ended. The documents found a decade ago suggested that no signing took place. I considered that a serious challenge, not a curiosity to be tucked into a footnote.”

He tapped the date on the copied decree. “The order from 863 showed that Aldric acted against mages after the supposed peace, but it did not name the Conclave. It could not settle the treaty question. On the evidence we had, I would teach 847 as the customary end of the war and 891, when Mira dissolved the Conclave, as the stronger candidate for its *formal* end. I would not call either conclusion certain.”

His beard twitched. “That was the truth as far as the surviving records allowed it. Now—did the next clause mention the Conclave?”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I squint at the decree, rereading the faded script.* "No, it doesn't mention the Conclave by name." I sigh, a little deflated. "It just says 'the rebellious factions'."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas gave the copy a disappointed look. “*The rebellious factions* identified no one. It did not connect the decree to the Conclave, and it did not establish that the Third Magical War continued in 863.”

He laid the decree beside the Veyrosi correspondence. “It remained worth cataloguing. But the western archive documents were the stronger evidence on the question that troubled you: they suggested Aldric’s treaty had been proposed, not signed. Until someone found an executed copy—or a convincing explanation for its absence—I favored 891 as the formal end. The textbook’s 847 remained the customary date, not a date beyond dispute.”

He pointed his stylus at the correspondence. “Now read the heading. The answer might have been sitting in front of us while we argued over a decree that named neither treaty nor Conclave.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod, chastened, and pick up the top scroll from the Veyrosi correspondence.* "Right, the Veyrosi correspondence." I clear my throat and begin to read. "Letter from Lord Valerius to King Aldric, concerning..." I trail off, eyes widening slightly. "...the ratification of the Treaty of Veyros."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas reached for the scroll, then stopped short of its brittle edge. His annoyance gave way to a scholar’s wary interest.

“*Concerning* ratification,” he said. “Not *confirming* ratification. A letter asking Aldric to ratify the treaty might support the western account; a letter acknowledging ratification might challenge it.”

He peered at the heading without quite bringing it into focus. “The date first. Then the opening lines, exactly as written. And do not turn a proposed treaty into a signed one merely because both appeared in the same sentence.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I carefully unroll the scroll, trying not to tear the old paper.* "It's dated 847 AE, the 17th of Fallowmonth. And it says... 'My Lord King, I humbly implore your Majesty's swift ratification of the enclosed Treaty of Veyros, that peace may finally be secured.'" My eyes dart up to his. "It *is* enclosed!"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas’s hand hovered over the scroll. “An enclosure was not an execution,” he said sharply. “Valerius *implored* Aldric to ratify it. On the seventeenth of Fallowmonth, at least, Valerius did not believe the treaty had secured peace.”

He leaned closer, squinting at the fold beneath the letter. “That supported the western documents rather better than your decree did. But it did not tell us whether Aldric ratified the treaty a week later—or whether the Conclave did. Nor could we yet say that the enclosure survived merely because the letter said one had been sent.”

He withdrew his hand from the brittle parchment. “Look for a separate sheet. If it was there, read its title before anything else. Then we shall examine its signatures and seals, not congratulate ourselves on finding the word *treaty*.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I gently slide the letter aside, revealing another, folded piece of parchment beneath.* "There's something here! It says... 'Treaty of Veyros, between King Aldric II and the Mage Conclave.'" My heart pounds a little. "It's the actual treaty!"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas’s stylus struck the desk with a sharp click. “It was a document *titled* ‘Treaty of Veyros.’ Whether it was an executed treaty remained to be seen.”

He leaned toward the folded parchment, his failing eyes narrowed. “Valerius’s letter asked for ratification. An enclosed copy was therefore quite possibly the text submitted *for* ratification, not proof that ratification occurred.”

He held out a hand but did not touch the sheet. “Read the final clause. Then tell me whose signatures and seals appeared beneath it, if any. The difference between a proposed peace and a concluded one lay at the bottom of that page.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I carefully unfold the second piece of parchment, my hands trembling slightly.* "Okay, at the very bottom... it says 'Witnessed by Lord Valerius, First Hand of the King'. And then... oh. There's only one seal." I look up, disappointed. "It's King Aldric's seal. No Conclave seal, no other signatures."

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Maester Tomas’s disappointment showed only in the tightening of his mouth. “Only one seal,” he repeated. “That was a finding. ‘The actual treaty’ was an inference, and a premature one.”

He bent toward the parchment, keeping his hands clear of its folds. “Aldric’s seal might indicate royal approval, if it was impressed upon this document at the proper time. But Valerius had asked the king to ratify an enclosed text, and nothing you have read showed that the Conclave accepted it. His witness mark did not stand in for theirs.”

He retrieved his stylus. “This complicated the western account: we could no longer say merely that an unsigned proposal survived. Yet it did not restore the textbook’s claim that both parties concluded peace in 847.” He pointed below the final clause. “Was there a space reserved for the Conclave’s seal? And what, precisely, did the clause say about when the treaty would take effect?”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I lean closer, tracing the faded lines with my finger.* "Yes, there's a blank space, clearly for another seal, and the text says 'This treaty shall take effect upon the affixing of the seal of the Mage Conclave.'" I glance up, a thought sparking. "So it was waiting for their seal?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
The archive smelled of old vellum and candle smoke. Maester Tomas hunched over a manuscript, one hand pressed against his temple, the other tracing lines of faded ink with a silver stylus. He did not look up when the apprentice entered.

"You're late. Again." His voice was dry. "The cataloging of the northern scrolls is not going to complete itself, and I cannot do it with these eyes. Begin with the Veyrosi correspondence."

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: I pull out my notes from the lecture last week. "Master Tomas, the lecture on the Third Magical War confused me. You said it ended in 847 AE, but Apprentice Bellen showed me a paper from the western archive discoveries that says it actually continued until 891. How is that possible?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas lifted his gaze from the manuscript, squinting as though the dates had been printed in especially malicious ink.

“Because ‘ended’ was an imprecise word—and, in this case, an old one.” He tapped the silver stylus against the page. “The accepted account held that Aldric II signed the Treaty of Veyros in 847 AE, ending the war. The western documents, however, indicated that the treaty was only proposed. No signature, no settlement.”

His mouth tightened. “The fighting dwindled into a cold state, which is not the same as peace. By the newer reckoning, the conflict persisted until Queen Mira dissolved the Mage Conclave in 891 AE. Bellen’s paper was not contradicting the evidence; it was contradicting the conventional chronology. I should have made that distinction clear in the lecture.”

dialogue.name: Apprentice
dialogue.content: *I nod slowly, absorbing this.* "So the history books... they're not always entirely accurate, then?" I gesture vaguely towards the shelves of scrolls. "Even the really old ones?"

dialogue.name: Maester Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas gave a dry, humorless sound. “Of course they were not always accurate. Age confers no immunity to error; it merely gives error more time to acquire a dignified binding.”

He set the stylus down, carefully, as if the manuscript might take offense. “But do not mistake that for saying every old book was worthless. A chronicle might preserve an eyewitness account and still misdate a treaty. A later copyist might ‘correct’ an unfamiliar name into a familiar one. And, in the case of Veyros, generations of scholars repeated the claim that Aldric signed the treaty in 847 because the conventional account said he had.”
